intro: Here the ancient and the modern live side by side. You are in Side, in Antalya province, a city whose story begins in the 7th century BC and whose ruins are woven into a modern town. Its fame rests on the Temple of Apollo, standing out on the point.
history: Side was a port, and a busy one: a major centre of the slave trade, with a language all its own. It grew into one of the largest cities of Pamphylia, and its theatre could seat 15,000 people. Imagine the noise of the harbour and the crowds that filled those seats.
structure-2: You are now at the Theatre, the largest in Pamphylia. Most ancient theatres lean against a hillside, but this one is rare: it was built on level ground, its cavea raised on a two-storey vaulted substructure. Its three-storey stage building once faced the colonnaded street of the city.
structure-3: Before you is the Monumental Fountain, the city's principal water-dispensing structure. Look for its decoration of gods and mythological figures, and imagine the water flowing past them into the life of the town.
structure-5: Here is the city gate, the monumental gateway in the city walls. Gates like this were often built in the form of a triumphal arch, so that arriving here was itself a small ceremony.
highlights: As you wander through Side, don't miss the Temple of Apollo, and make time for the Agora as well.
facts: Did you know? Side is remembered as one of the places where Cleopatra met Mark Antony. Its very name means 'pomegranate' in the local Anatolian language. In Roman times it held one of the Mediterranean's largest slave markets, where pirates sold what they had taken. And today, at sunset, the seaward columns of the Temple of Apollo have become the emblem of the city.
outro: This brings our tour of Side to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these ruins keep their story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
